text: dsh-delivery-board 是面向 DSH 的代码库交付管理插件，提供工具、命令和本机网页看板。它把项目阶段、负责人、卡片、验收标准、DoD 清单与交接日志保存在工作区的 delivery.json 中，并可用 skill 辅助自然语言规划。主要功能包括创建和调整阶段流水线、添加与更新工作卡、跨阶段流转并留存审计、查看 Kanban 与 Timeline、生成客户周报，以及记录和解决风险阻塞。适合希望把单仓库交付状态随 Git 管理的项目团队和编码 agent。插件不要求 API key 或外部账号；交互看板按需在本机环回地址启动。

dsh-delivery-board is a DSH plugin for managing delivery stages, cards, and handoffs in a repository. It offers a local board, Timeline, and weekly reports, with state stored in delivery.json. Teams and coding agents can track work without an external account.
想把项目的阶段、负责人和交付卡片跟代码一起放进仓库管理。
有没有办法记录每张任务卡从一个阶段交给下一个阶段的过程？
让 DSH 根据工作卡片和本周进展整理一份客户周报。
我想在浏览器里拖动卡片、编辑内容并查看项目时间线。
I need a lightweight way to track delivery stages, owners, and handoffs in a Git repository.
Can I turn project activity into a weekly client report with shipped work and open blockers?
dsh-delivery-board 的功能「交付阶段与卡片」：通过 DSH 工具创建项目、添加工作卡并维护阶段流水线；卡片可记录负责人、日期、验收标准和 DoD。
dsh-delivery-board 的功能「交接审计」：用 delivery_move 或看板移动卡片到其他阶段时，更新阶段并自动写入 handoff 日志，可同时更换负责人和附加备注。
dsh-delivery-board 的功能「周报生成」：调用 delivery_weekly 或 /delivery-admin weekly，按指定周汇总阶段快照、交付项、交接、未解决风险和已解决风险，并可附上下周计划。
dsh-delivery-board 的功能「本机交互看板」：调用 delivery_open 获取环回地址，在浏览器查看 Kanban、Timeline 和归档视图，并拖动或编辑卡片后保存回同一份工作区状态。
dsh-delivery-board 的功能「风险与阻塞记录」：调用 delivery_log 记录进展、风险、阻塞或决策，再用 delivery_resolve 按日志索引标记风险或阻塞已解决。
dsh-delivery-board 使用前须知：交互看板会按需在本机 127.0.0.1 启动服务，并读写工作区里的 delivery.json；该服务在插件停止或 DSH 退出时关闭。
如何给交付流程设置阶段，并在项目变化时调整或迁移卡片？
想把完成清单、风险和阻塞都记在同一份项目交付状态里。

> **Plan, owners, status, and handoff history in one JSON file next to your code** — no SaaS, no account; reviewed in every PR.

The board is just a view. PM and engineers trust the same `delivery.json`: stages, WIP, weekly report, and an audit of moves that actually happened — so management and delivery work off one shared context, versioned with the repo.

dsh-delivery-board README · Why it exists：From Plan through requirements, design, build, test, and go-live, if delivery state is not alongside the code, people and agents struggle to stay aligned: who owns what, what “done” means, and where work is stuck often live only in handoffs and verbal sync.

dsh-delivery-board README · Why it exists：**dsh-delivery-board** writes the stage pipeline, handoff trail, and client weekly report into in-repo delivery state (`delivery.json` by default). The kanban board, calendar Timeline, audit log, and weekly Markdown report are projections of that same state — not a separate SaaS. PMs, engineers, QA, and AI agents share one Source of Truth that travels with the repo.

dsh-delivery-board README · Compared to alternatives：| Need | This project | Typical SaaS kanban | Markdown checklists alone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lives in the git repo | Yes (`delivery.json`) | Usually a remote workspace | Yes, but no structured handoffs / WIP |
| Handoff audit + weekly client report | Built-in | Needs custom fields / exports | Manual |
| Local editable UI + Timeline | Loopback board | Full web app | No |
| Works with AI coding agents | DSH skill + tools; CLI for any agent/shell | Often via API / MCP | Prompt-only |
| Scope | Delivery context for one repo | Org-wide PM suite | Lightweight notes |

dsh-delivery-board README · Compared to alternatives：It is intentionally **not** a rebuild of Jira, Linear, or Notion — those are excellent for org-scale planning. This keeps only the delivery context the current repository actually needs, offline-friendly and reviewable in PRs.

If this saves your team a standup or a messy weekly paste, a [⭐ star](https://github.com/jerryxff26-alt/delivery-board) helps others find it — thank you.

dsh-delivery-board README · Design principles：- **Delivery state is a first-class citizen** — stages, owners, acceptance criteria (AC), Definition of Done (DoD), handoffs, and blockers live in the repo and evolve with Git.
- **Views are projections** — the local board, handoff audit, client weekly report, and offline HTML are all projections of the same delivery state.
- **Operate via CLI or DSH** — advance stages, fill in AC, log blockers, and generate weekly reports with `npx github:jerryxff26-alt/delivery-board …` (or `npx dsh-delivery-board …` after npm publish), `/delivery`, or plain language; you do not treat JSON as the day-to-day editing UI.
- **Clear boundaries** — this is not a rebuild of an enterprise project-management platform; it keeps in the codebase only the delivery context the current repo actually needs.

dsh-delivery-board README · What you get：- **Stage pipeline + cards** — each card has an owner, optional description, optional `start`/`due` dates, acceptance criteria and a checkable Definition of Done (DoD) checklist. Stages can be added, renamed or removed after init (removing refuses while cards remain unless you migrate them).
- **Handoff audit trail** — moving a card to another stage records who handed what to whom, automatically.
- **Weekly report** — a Markdown client report: pipeline snapshot, **shipped this week** (arrived at the terminal stage or archived), handoffs, open risks, and **risks resolved this week**. Optional `next_week` notes appear as **Next bets** (omitted when empty).
- **Soft WIP limits** — optional per-stage `wipLimit` (Kanban-style). The board and move responses warn when a stage is over; moves are never blocked.
- **Local editable board** — ask `/delivery Open the editable board`; the tool serves a mouse drag-and-drop board on `127.0.0.1` that saves back to the same delivery state. Archive/restore, risk/blocker logging, and per-card DoD checklists are available on the board. Accessibility fallback: Edit → Stage. Board chrome follows the browser locale

dsh-delivery-board README · Primary path (usual four steps)：1. **Initialize** — `lite` template (or `/delivery Initialize a lite board for ACME`)
2. **Create a card** — outcome + stage (CLI `card` / `/delivery Add a card…`)
3. **Hand off** — move across stages (`move` / `/delivery Hand off…`); open the local board when you want drag-and-drop
4. **Weekly / open** — `weekly` for the client report, `open` for the live board

dsh-delivery-board README · Primary path (usual four steps)：`/delivery` = model-led skill (normal day-to-day). `/delivery-admin` = deterministic, no-model escape hatch. Prefer `/delivery` unless you need a scriptable command.

dsh-delivery-board README · Primary path (usual four steps)：**Quiet board / ready for daily use (v0.3.0):** Polish-freeze. Touch gets a quiet always-visible ⋯ overlay (`hover: none` only); desktop stays hover. Timeline + Archive + editor share the same near-black / 8px / hairline language. Archive cards match active chrome (title+meta; Restore in ⋯). Handoff audit logs **only actual stage moves** (A→C is one line; intentional skips are not logged as intermediate hops).

dsh-delivery-board README · Primary path (usual four steps)：**Title+meta cards (v0.2.7):** Kanban cards at rest show only title and meta (owner/due/blocked) — no reserved ID/drag/⋯ strip. The ⋯ menu is an absolute hover/focus overlay. Cursor grab is the drag affordance; IDs stay in aria/edit/copy. Touch screenshots stay clean (no forced chrome). Zero CDN fonts / no new deps.

dsh-delivery-board README · Primary path (usual four steps)：**Quiet premium UI (v0.2.6):** Near-black Linear-like primary (no SaaS purple), flatter 8px hairline cards, Active/Timeline/Archive segments without counts, quiet Saved status, short subtitle (template · N cards), blocked as meta/left hairline, Risks collapsed by default.

**Calmer board UI (v0.2.4):** softer palette, thin muted stage accents, roomier cards, AC/DoD as quiet chips, Edit/Archive/Copy behind a ⋯ menu.

dsh-delivery-board README · Primary path (usual four steps)：**Less friction (v0.2.3):** stages/cards accept **id or name/title** (case-insensitive, unique; errors list candidates). Positional CLI works: `init ACME lite`, `card API doing Ada`, `move API review`. Open risks stay visible on the board.

dsh-delivery-board README · Model-led skill (normal workflow)：The plugin bundles and registers a **`delivery` skill**. Type `/delivery` followed by the outcome you want; DSH loads its instructions into the model instead of parsing a direct command. No separate skill copy/install is needed. Plain-language requests can also discover the skill through DSH's skill catalog.

dsh-delivery-board README · Model-led skill (normal workflow)：```text
/delivery Review this repository and propose a delivery plan for ACME from its requirements and tests.
/delivery Create the cards from the approved plan; leave unknown owners and dates unset.
/delivery Hand off the API integration card to Test, assign Morgan, and summarize the available evidence.
/delivery Open the editable board.

dsh-delivery-board README · Model-led skill (normal workflow)：The skill reads relevant repository context, identifies gaps, and generates stages, card content, acceptance criteria and DoD. It proposes a substantial plan before bulk creation. The existing `delivery_*` tools then validate inputs, save state, record handoffs and render views. **The model reasons; the tools persist.** `delivery_init` itself still creates an empty project deterministically; the skill orchestrates card creation after plan approval.

dsh-delivery-board README · Model-led skill (normal workflow)：This is a **skill backed by the existing plugin**, not a prompt that edits JSON directly. The JSON schema, board UI and model-facing tool names are unchanged. Project-local skills can override the packaged skill using DSH's normal skill precedence.

dsh-delivery-board README · Advanced direct controls (no model call)：The former native `/delivery` command is now **`/delivery-admin`**, so it cannot intercept skill prompts. Existing direct command examples or scripts must change their prefix; delivery data does not need migration.

dsh-delivery-board README · Advanced direct controls (no model call)：`board --archived` includes archived cards. `init`, `card`, `update` and `log` take JSON objects; `move` also accepts JSON for owner changes and handoff notes. These advanced commands still delegate to the same validated tools.

dsh-delivery-board README · Advanced direct controls (no model call)：For linked desktop development, fully quit and reopen DSH after updating the plugin. It needs DSH's `skills` service and `tool-skill` loader (supported by the tested 0.2.1-rc.2 runtime). Confirm the plugin shows **Running**. `/delivery <request>` is handled as a skill; `/delivery-admin` uses the direct command handler.

dsh-delivery-board README · Pipeline templates：| Template | Stages |
|---|---|
| **`lite` (Lite Pipeline)** — recommended quickstart | Backlog → Doing → Review → Live |
| `default` (ToB Delivery Pipeline) | Client Requirements → BA Analysis → TL Design → Development → Testing → DevSecOps Launch → Live |
| `governance` (Governance Pipeline) | Plan → Analyze → Design → Build → Test → Deploy → Live |

dsh-delivery-board README · Pipeline templates：Fully custom stages are supported via the `stages` parameter. Prefer `lite` unless you need the longer ToB or governance pipelines. (Legacy files that still contain per-stage `gates` / `gateDone` load fine — those fields are dropped on validate.)

dsh-delivery-board README · Tools：| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `delivery_init` | Initialize a project (prefer `lite`; or `default` / `governance` / custom stages) |
| `delivery_card` | Add a card: title, stage, owner, optional start/due, description, acceptance criteria, DoD checklist |
| `delivery_move` | Move a card to another stage (records a handoff; owner can change). Same-stage owner changes are recorded as a decision, not a handoff |
| `delivery_board` | Quick text board; excludes archived cards unless requested |
| `delivery_open` | Editable local board URL (drag, create/edit) |
| `delivery_update` | Edit title, owner, start/due, description, acceptance and DoD without moving |
| `delivery_log` | Log progress / risk / blocker / decision |
| `delivery_weekly` | Client weekly report (Markdown): shipped / handoffs / open & resolved risks / next bets |

dsh-delivery-board README · Tools：| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `delivery_archive` / `delivery_restore` | Hide a card without deleting history / return it to its original stage |
| `delivery_archive_board` | Snapshot the whole board to `delivery-archive/…`, then reset an empty board (same pipeline) |
| `delivery_dod_add` / `delivery_dod_check` | Append a DoD checklist item / tick or untick an item (never blocks moves) |
| `delivery_board_html` | Read-only standalone HTML snapshot |
| `delivery_resolve` | Mark an open risk/blocker log entry resolved by index |
| `delivery_stage_add` / `delivery_stage_update` / `delivery_stage_remove` | Evolve the pipeline after init (remove requires `migrate_to` if cards remain; stages accept optional soft `wip_limit`) |

dsh-delivery-board README · Editable local board vs offline HTML：- `delivery_open` (via the skill, or `/delivery-admin open`) returns a URL. **Drag cards** between stage columns to move them (primary UX); use **Edit → Stage** as the accessibility fallback. Create/edit cards, archive/restore. Saves go to the same in-repo delivery state and audit history.
- The live server starts on demand, binds only to `127.0.0.1` on an ephemeral port and uses an unguessable capability path. Treat the URL as private to your machine; it expires when the plugin unloads or DSH exits.
- If another tab, command or external edit changes the state file, a stale page cannot silently overwrite it: press **Refresh** and retry (conflict protection, not live sync).
- `/delivery-admin html` writes a read-only `.html`/`.htm` file with search, owner filter and archive view; it cannot overwrite the data file.

text: dsh-delivery-board README · Team collaboration：Commit `delivery.json` (the on-disk delivery state) to the team's shared git repo; `git pull`/`push` is the sync. Concurrent edits still need normal Git conflict review. Each stage renders up to 30 cards initially with **Load more**; search and owner filters cover the whole file.

Implementation notes:

dsh-delivery-board README · Development：- Plugin contract `name / inject / Config / apply`; tools via `defineTool`; the bundled `skills/delivery/SKILL.md` is registered through `ctx.skills.register`. Tool output renderers return `ContentBlock[]`.
- Domain logic (`lib/delivery.js`) and the HTML renderer (`lib/board-html.js`) are pure functions; all writes go through `lib/store.js`. The DSH plugin uses `ctx.fs`; the standalone CLI uses `lib/node-fs.js` + `lib/standalone.js` with the same store contract.
- Weekly reports cover seven local-calendar days starting at `week_start` (default: Monday of the current week). **Shipped** = handoffs into the terminal pipeline stage or archives in that window; open risks are listed; **Risks resolved this week** uses `resolvedAt` in the window. Pass `next_week` notes to include a **Next bets** section (omitted when empty).
- Per-card **DoD** is a checkable checklist (`{text, done, doneBy?, doneAt?}`); ticking never blocks moves. Legacy string/list DoD migrates on load.
- Soft **WIP limits** (`wipLimit` / tool field `wip_limit`) are optional per stage; over-limit stages warn on the board and after moves, but never refuse a move.

dsh-delivery-board README · Practice notes (lightweight)：Drawn from delivery practices that fit an in-repo board without becoming a PM suite:

- **Kanban soft WIP** — set `wip_limit` on busy stages so overload is visible.
- **Weekly shipped / next bets** — Shape Up-flavored cadence: what landed, what burned down, what you are betting on next (still just Markdown + YAML/JSON state).

dsh-delivery-board README · Won't build：- Hard-blocking DoD/WIP (no process engine)
- Multi-project / multi-workspace rollup or org portfolio
- Cloud notifications, email/IM push, accounts, or SSO
- Custom-field sprawl / multiple issue-type systems
- Dual Track discovery↔delivery modules, DoR, or appetite as productized methodology packs
- Realtime multi-user CRDT sync, Gantt resource loading, burn-down suites
- Promoting every admin subcommand into a first-class agent tool

dsh-delivery-board README · Possible later (not promises)：- Embed the editable board inside DSH (standalone CLI already ships)
- Fuller i18n for reports and tool messages (board chrome already follows browser locale)

dsh-delivery-board README · Known limitations：- **Standalone CLI** needs only Node ≥20 (`npx github:jerryxff26-alt/delivery-board` now; `npx dsh-delivery-board` after npm publish). The DSH plugin path is a developer preview: `engines.dsh >=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`; peers `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools >=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery ~3.18.5` (host-provided, optional). Smoke-tested on DSH 0.2.1-rc.2; previously verified on 0.2.0-rc.2.
- No full Gantt resource loading, hard move-blocking DoD/WIP, or realtime multi-user sync. Whole-board archive is a deliberate snapshot+reset, not automatic bulk archive.
- Drag/drop (and Edit → Stage fallback) are checked in a local browser harness; no full keyboard/mobile/WCAG claim.
- DoD checklists and WIP limits are soft signals only; moving a card does not require DoD items to be checked or WIP to be under limit.
- Empty columns and uninitialized projects point at **one** next step (`init` / `delivery_init` / `/delivery …`, or **New card** on the board).
